chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no nobility for a Qureyshite nor for an Arab except through humility, and there is no prestige except through piety, and there is no deed except through intention, and there is no worship except through understanding. Indeed, the most hateful of people to Allah is the one who emulates the Sunnah of an Imam but does not emulate him in his deeds.
ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions for true nobility and worship according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes that true nobility (Karam) and social standing are derived not from lineage but from humility (Tawadu') and piety (Taqwa), while valid worship requires both sincere intention (Niyyah) and deep jurisprudential understanding (Tafquh). It concludes by critiquing superficial imitation, warning that the most disliked to Allah are those who follow an Imam's outward Sunnah without emulating his substantive actions and character. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam as a living model of both doctrine and practice, rather than a mere source of ritual precedent.
